automationStatus: No automated feed or polling is connected. Each row is a dated manual review of a public source.

entries.accessNote: This entry uses the open press-center article only. TrendForce's linked detailed reports may require a subscription.
entries.evidence: TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices up 10-15% quarter over quarter in 4Q26, NAND flash up 15-20%, and enterprise SSD price growth accelerating. It projects enterprise SSD bit demand above 80% year over year in 2026. These are forecasts, not realized prices.
entries.operatingMetricImplication: Compare realized DRAM and NAND ASPs with bits shipped, inventory, and product mix. Enterprise SSD strength can lift NAND mix and supplier pricing, while lower client SSD capacity and cautious module-maker buying can limit consumer-side bits.

entries.accessNote: This entry uses the open press-center article only. Linked detailed reports may require a subscription.
entries.evidence: TrendForce revised its 2027 HBM blended ASP outlook to +121% year over year, citing persistent supply constraints and a larger HBM4 mix. It says 8-high stacks may carry a 10-20% premium per gigabit to 12-high stacks as vendors consider using fewer HBM layers per accelerator.
entries.operatingMetricImplication: Track HBM revenue and bits separately, stack-height mix, HBM4 qualification and yields, and customer accelerator configurations. A higher ASP forecast can coexist with lower HBM capacity per accelerator and does not by itself prove supplier unit growth.

entries.companyOrMarket: H100 and Blackwell B200/GB200 rental pricing
entries.sourceKind: Public aggregator; provider-stated live API inputs
entries.accessNote: Public page, no account required for the displayed index. The provider says index inputs come from public APIs and excludes static rate cards.
entries.evidence: The page displayed H100 at $2.78 per GPU-hour from 45 sources and Blackwell B200/GB200 at $6.19 per GPU-hour from 11 sources. Its page timestamp was 2026-10-11 01:25:14 UTC when reviewed on 2026-10-13. The page says it fetches inputs every 60 seconds, but the chart data was still loading during review and the displayed observations were about two days old.
entries.operatingMetricImplication: Use GPU-hour prices as a directional input to cloud compute cost, gross margin, and customer payback scenarios. Check source-level timestamps, spot/on-demand mix, utilization, and realized discounts before translating index moves into a provider's revenue or margin.
entries.freshnessCaveat: The provider claims 60-second refresh, but this review only verified the page timestamp and displayed values. No independent API polling or history capture is implemented here.

entries.companyOrMarket: SEMCO, Japanese suppliers, Taiwanese and Chinese suppliers
entries.changeType: OEM price estimate and supply allocation
entries.accessNote: This entry uses the open press-center article only. Linked detailed reports may require a subscription.
entries.evidence: TrendForce estimates SEMCO's 4Q26 OEM/ODM consumer X5R price increase at 25-30% and high-end AI/server X6S at 10-20%, depending on negotiation. The article says Murata, Taiyo Yuden, and Kyocera were then holding prices unchanged. Estimates are not supplier-confirmed price notices.
entries.operatingMetricImplication: Watch realized ASP by dielectric and capacitance, utilization, orders, and high-end mix. Consumer price hikes may be used to ration orders and free capacity, so higher ASP need not mean higher unit volume; confirmation by Japanese suppliers would test whether increases are broadening.

entries.companyOrMarket: Murata RCE and RDE lead-type MLCCs for 48V systems
entries.accessNote: Public product announcement. No account required to read the cited specifications.
entries.evidence: Murata announced a 100Vdc, 10μF lead-type MLCC in its RCE and RDE series and said mass production began in August 2026. It positions the part for automotive and consumer/industrial 48V systems, including higher-output equipment.
entries.operatingMetricImplication: This is a product-mix and addressable-content signal, not proof of material revenue. Follow qualification, design wins, production volume, and automotive or industrial customer mix in later disclosures.

entries.companyOrMarket: AT&S high-end IC substrates for AI and high-performance computing
entries.accessNote: Public company release. AT&S's broader product materials identify ABF substrates in its portfolio, but this expansion notice says high-end IC substrates and does not specify ABF material for the new capacity.
entries.evidence: AT&S said it decided to expand Chongqing capacity for a key customer's high-end IC substrates, with investment in the high double-digit millions of euros and long-term customer agreements. The release expected a high double-digit million euro EBIT contribution in FY2026/27, about €400m total FY2026/27 capex, 30-35% currency-adjusted revenue growth, and a 25-29% EBITDA margin. The notice does not break out ABF-specific capacity or economics.
entries.operatingMetricImplication: Track substrate sales, customer qualification, capacity utilization, capex, depreciation, and EBIT as the expansion ramps. Customer-backed funding may reduce financing pressure, but the stated growth and EBIT contribution are management expectations rather than realized ABF revenue.

entries.accessNote: Public company release. It describes high-performance IC package substrates for AI and high-performance servers but does not explicitly identify the material as ABF in this notice.
entries.evidence: IBIDEN outlined approximately ¥500bn of electronics-business capex over FY2026-FY2028, including a planned approximately ¥220bn first phase centered on Gama Plant Cell6. Sequential operation and mass production were planned to begin from FY2027. This is a capacity plan, not a current production observation.
entries.operatingMetricImplication: Compare capex and construction milestones with qualification, utilization, depreciation, substrate shipments, and cash generation. The time lag to mass production means investment announcements should not be booked as near-term shipment growth.
